    write_json("student_profiles.json", profiles)
    write_json("synthetic_profiles.json", synthetic)

    REVIEW_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    review.extend([
        {"item_type": "source_discrepancy", "item_id": "SL302/CSL302", "issue": "The semester table on PDF p. 21 prints SL302; p. 22 and catalogue p. 84 print CSL302.", "source_page": "21,22,84"},
        {"item_type": "prerequisite_code", "item_id": "CSP352:IC100", "issue": "Prerequisite printed as IC100 on PDF p. 86; no matching course entry was located in the 208-page PDF.", "source_page": 86},
        {"item_type": "policy_gap", "item_id": "CS-minor", "issue": "No CS-minor eligibility, curriculum, or credit pathway is stated in the supplied PDF.", "source_page": "full PDF"},
        {"item_type": "policy_gap", "item_id": "semester-credit-limits", "issue": "No minimum/maximum semester credits or overload rule was found; current values remain assumptions pending ordinance.", "source_page": "full PDF"},
        {"item_type": "policy_gap", "item_id": "course-offering-and-elective-eligibility", "issue": "Catalogue-only courses have no BTech CSE semester slot; annual availability and elective eligibility remain assumptions.", "source_page": "9,22,83-95"},
    ])
    with REVIEW_PATH.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as file:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(file, fieldnames=["item_type", "item_id", "issue", "source_page"])
        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerows(review)

    print(f"Built {len(courses)} courses, {len(skills)} skills, {len(modules)} modules, {len(exercises)} original exercises, {len(resources)} OERs.")
    print(f"Built {len(profiles)} hero personas and {len(synthetic)} synthetic profiles.")
    print(f"Review queue contains {len(review)} unresolved item(s).")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    build_seed()

         "correct": "Floyd-Warshall algorithm",
         "explanation": "Floyd-Warshall iteratively updates dist[i][j] = min(dist[i][j], dist[i][k] + dist[k][j]) across all k in O(V^3)."}, 83)
    add("ex_algo_10", "algorithms", "mod_csl202_4", "mcq", 4,
        "What is the approximation ratio of the standard greedy 2-approximation algorithm for the Vertex Cover problem?",
        {"options": ["2", "1.5", "log n", "1.33"],
         "correct": "2",
         "explanation": "Taking both endpoints of maximal matching edges yields a vertex cover whose size is at most 2 * OPT."}, 83)

    # 6. computer_architecture (ECL101, p. 21)
    add("ex_arch_01", "computer_architecture", "mod_ecl101_1", "mcq", 1,
        "In basic digital logic, what is the output of an XOR gate when both inputs are 1?",
        {"options": ["0", "1", "High-impedance", "Indeterminate"],
         "correct": "0",
         "explanation": "XOR produces 1 only when inputs differ. 1 XOR 1 = 0."}, 21)
    add("ex_arch_02", "computer_architecture", "mod_ecl101_1", "mcq", 1,
        "What role does the Program Counter (PC) register perform in a CPU?",
        {"options": ["Holds memory address of the next instruction to execute",
                     "Stores the outcome of the Arithmetic Logic Unit",
                     "Tracks the current stack frame pointer",
                     "Holds memory bus parity bits"],
         "correct": "Holds memory address of the next instruction to execute",
         "explanation": "The PC register holds the address of the next sequential instruction fetched from instruction memory."}, 21)
    add("ex_arch_03", "computer_architecture", "mod_ecl101_2", "mcq", 2,
        "What is a Data Hazard in an instruction execution pipeline?",
        {"options": ["An instruction depends on the result of a prior instruction still in the pipeline",
                     "Two instructions compete for the same hardware functional unit simultaneously",
                     "A branch instruction changes program counter flow",
                     "A parity error occurs during memory bus transfer"],
         "correct": "An instruction depends on the result of a prior instruction still in the pipeline",
         "explanation": "Data hazards occur when read-after-write (RAW), write-after-read (WAR), or write-after-write (WAW) dependencies stall execution."}, 21)
    add("ex_arch_04", "computer_architecture", "mod_ecl101_2", "short", 2,
        "If a 5-stage pipeline has ideal CPI of 1.0, what maximum speedup does it theoretically approach over a non-pipelined single-cycle processor?",
        {"correct": "5x",
         "rubric": "5x speedup 5 stages throughput pipelining",
         "explanation": "Under ideal conditions with continuous instruction flow and balanced stages, an n-stage pipeline approaches an n-fold speedup (5x)."}, 21)
    add("ex_arch_05", "computer_architecture", "mod_ecl101_2", "mcq", 2,
        "Which architectural technique mitigates control hazards by predicting whether a conditional branch will be taken?",
        {"options": ["Dynamic branch prediction", "Operand forwarding", "Loop unrolling", "Memory interleaving"],
         "correct": "Dynamic branch prediction",
         "explanation": "Branch prediction speculatively fetches instructions based on branch history tables before condition resolution."}, 21)
    add("ex_arch_06", "computer_architecture", "mod_ecl101_3", "mcq", 3,
        "In a direct-mapped cache, how is a memory address partitioned into fields?",
        {"options": ["Tag, Index, and Block Offset", "Tag and Offset only", "Set, Page, and Offset", "Base, Limit, and Offset"],
         "correct": "Tag, Index, and Block Offset",
         "explanation": "A direct-mapped cache address splits into Block Offset (within line), Index (selects line), and Tag (confirms identity)."}, 21)
    add("ex_arch_07", "computer_architecture", "mod_ecl101_3", "mcq", 3,
        "What is the formula for Average Memory Access Time (AMAT)?",
        {"options": ["Hit Time + (Miss Rate * Miss Penalty)",
                     "Hit Rate * Hit Time + Miss Penalty",
                     "Miss Rate * Miss Penalty",
                     "Hit Time / (1 - Miss Rate)"],
         "correct": "Hit Time + (Miss Rate * Miss Penalty)",
         "explanation": "AMAT accounts for L1 hit latency plus the expected latency penalty incurred on a cache miss."}, 21)
    add("ex_arch_08", "computer_architecture", "mod_ecl101_3", "mcq", 3,
        "Which cache replacement policy evicts the block that has remained unreferenced for the longest elapsed time?",
        {"options": ["Least Recently Used (LRU)", "First-In-First-Out (FIFO)", "Random Replacement", "Most Recently Used (MRU)"],
         "correct": "Least Recently Used (LRU)",
         "explanation": "LRU exploits temporal locality by discarding items not accessed for the longest period."}, 21)
    add("ex_arch_09", "computer_architecture", "mod_ecl101_3", "mcq", 4,
        "What is the primary function of a Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB)?",
        {"options": ["Cache recent virtual-to-physical address translations to avoid multi-level page table walks",
                     "Cache instruction branch target addresses",
                     "Buffer dirty cache lines before writing to main memory",
                     "Store vector register operands"],
         "correct": "Cache recent virtual-to-physical address translations to avoid multi-level page table walks",
         "explanation": "The TLB is a dedicated MMU cache storing recently resolved virtual-to-physical page frame translations."}, 21)
    add("ex_arch_10", "computer_architecture", "mod_ecl101_3", "mcq", 4,
        "In Tomasulo's out-of-order execution algorithm, what hardware structure holds operands and operation codes waiting for execution units?",
        {"options": ["Reservation Stations", "Reorder Buffer only", "Register Allocation Table", "Branch Target Buffer"],
         "correct": "Reservation Stations",
         "explanation": "Reservation stations buffer instructions and listen on the Common Data Bus (CDB) for operand values to resolve hazards."}, 21)

    # 7. theory_computation (CSL253, p. 84)
    add("ex_toc_01", "theory_computation", "mod_csl253_1", "mcq", 1,
        "What class of formal languages is recognized by Deterministic Finite Automata (DFA)?",
        {"options": ["Regular languages", "Context-free languages", "Context-sensitive languages", "Recursively enumerable languages"],
         "correct": "Regular languages",
         "explanation": "DFAs, NFAs, and regular expressions recognize exactly the class of regular languages."}, 84)
    add("ex_toc_02", "theory_computation", "mod_csl253_1", "mcq", 1,
        "Which of the following operations is NOT closed under the family of regular languages?",
        {"options": ["Infinite union", "Finite union", "Intersection", "Complementation"],
         "correct": "Infinite union",
         "explanation": "Regular languages are closed under finite union, concatenation, Kleene star, intersection, and complement, but not infinite union."}, 84)
    add("ex_toc_03", "theory_computation", "mod_csl253_2", "mcq", 2,
        "What is the computational equivalence between Non-deterministic Finite Automata (NFA) and Deterministic Finite Automata (DFA)?",
        {"options": ["NFAs and DFAs recognize the exact same class of regular languages",
                     "NFAs can recognize non-regular languages that DFAs cannot",
                     "DFAs are strictly more powerful than NFAs",
                     "NFAs can recognize context-free languages"],
         "correct": "NFAs and DFAs recognize the exact same class of regular languages",
         "explanation": "Via the subset construction algorithm, any NFA with n states can be converted into an equivalent DFA with at most 2^n states."}, 84)
    add("ex_toc_04", "theory_computation", "mod_csl253_2", "mcq", 2,
        "Which formal grammar class in the Chomsky hierarchy generates Context-Free Languages (CFLs)?",
        {"options": ["Type 2 grammars", "Type 0 grammars", "Type 1 grammars", "Type 3 grammars"],
         "correct": "Type 2 grammars",
         "explanation": "Chomsky Type 2 grammars have productions of the form A -> alpha where A is a non-terminal, generating CFLs."}, 84)
    add("ex_toc_05", "theory_computation", "mod_csl253_3", "short", 2,
        "What auxiliary memory mechanism distinguishes a Pushdown Automaton (PDA) from a standard Finite Automaton?",
        {"correct": "stack",
         "rubric": "stack push pop lifo auxiliary memory",
         "explanation": "A Pushdown Automaton is equipped with an unbounded LIFO stack memory allowing it to count matching symbols."}, 84)
    add("ex_toc_06", "theory_computation", "mod_csl253_3", "mcq", 3,
        "The language L = {a^n b^n | n >= 0} is proved to be non-regular using which mathematical lemma?",
        {"options": ["Pumping Lemma for regular languages", "Rice's Theorem", "Cook-Levin Theorem", "Church-Turing Thesis"],
         "correct": "Pumping Lemma for regular languages",
         "explanation": "The Pumping Lemma for regular languages shows that any regular language can be pumped; pumping a^p b^p violates the form."}, 84)
    add("ex_toc_07", "theory_computation", "mod_csl253_4", "mcq", 3,
        "When applying the Pumping Lemma for regular languages with pumping length p to string s = xyz, which condition is mandatory?",
        {"options": ["|xy| <= p and |y| >= 1", "|xyz| < p", "|y| = 0", "|x| = |z|"],
         "correct": "|xy| <= p and |y| >= 1",
         "explanation": "The lemma mandates that the first p characters contain the pumpable substring y, requiring |xy| <= p and |y| >= 1."}, 84)
    add("ex_toc_08", "theory_computation", "mod_csl253_3", "mcq", 3,
        "What did Alan Turing establish regarding the Halting Problem for Turing machines?",
        {"options": ["It is undecidable by any algorithm",
                     "It is solvable in exponential time",
                     "It is solvable only for deterministic machines",
                     "It is solvable if memory is infinite"],
         "correct": "It is undecidable by any algorithm",
         "explanation": "Turing used Cantor diagonalization to prove that no Turing machine can decide whether arbitrary programs halt on arbitrary inputs."}, 84)
    add("ex_toc_09", "theory_computation", "mod_csl253_4", "mcq", 4,
        "According to Rice's Theorem, which semantic properties of Turing-recognizable languages are algorithmically decidable?",
        {"options": ["Only trivial properties (satisfied by all or no recognizable languages)",
                     "All properties involving finite strings",
                     "Emptiness and equivalence only",
                     "Properties verifiable in polynomial time"],
         "correct": "Only trivial properties (satisfied by all or no recognizable languages)",
         "explanation": "Rice's Theorem proves that any non-trivial semantic property of the language of a Turing machine is undecidable."}, 84)
    add("ex_toc_10", "theory_computation", "mod_csl253_4", "mcq", 4,
        "If language A is polynomial-time reducible to language B (A <=p B), and language B is known to be in P, what follows?",
        {"options": ["Language A is in P", "Language A is NP-complete", "Language B is NP-hard", "Language A is undecidable"],
         "correct": "Language A is in P",
         "explanation": "Since reduction takes polynomial time and solving B takes polynomial time, A can be solved in polynomial time: A in P."}, 84)

    # 8. operating_systems (CSL301, p. 84)
    add("ex_os_01", "operating_systems", "mod_csl301_1", "mcq", 1,
        "What state does a running process enter when it executes a blocking read() system call?",
        {"options": ["Waiting / Blocked state", "Ready state", "Terminated state", "Zombie state"],
         "correct": "Waiting / Blocked state",
         "explanation": "When awaiting an I/O event or resource, the kernel transitions the process to the Waiting/Blocked queue."}, 84)
    add("ex_os_02", "operating_systems", "mod_csl301_1", "mcq", 1,
        "What is the primary function of the operating system kernel?",
        {"options": ["Manage core hardware resources (CPU, memory, devices) and provide privileged system services",
                     "Render the graphical desktop environment",
                     "Compile user C programs into machine code",
                     "Format web pages for browser display"],
         "correct": "Manage core hardware resources (CPU, memory, devices) and provide privileged system services",
         "explanation": "The kernel is the core privileged program managing CPU scheduling, memory mapping, and device communication."}, 84)
    add("ex_os_03", "operating_systems", "mod_csl301_2", "mcq", 2,
        "In Round-Robin CPU scheduling, what happens if the time quantum is configured much larger than process burst times?",
        {"options": ["It degenerates into First-Come-First-Served (FCFS) scheduling",
                     "It degenerates into Shortest Job First (SJF)",
                     "Context switching overhead increases catastrophically",
                     "Processes experience starvation"],
         "correct": "It degenerates into First-Come-First-Served (FCFS) scheduling",
         "explanation": "If time quantum q exceeds maximum burst time, every process completes in its first allocation, identical to FCFS."}, 84)
    add("ex_os_04", "operating_systems", "mod_csl301_2", "mcq", 2,
        "What condition constitutes a race condition in multi-threaded programming?",
        {"options": ["Multiple concurrent threads access shared state without synchronization and at least one access is a write",
                     "Two threads read the same memory location simultaneously",
                     "A thread sleeps while waiting for a network packet",
                     "Thread priority inversion occurs on single-core systems"],
         "correct": "Multiple concurrent threads access shared state without synchronization and at least one access is a write",
         "explanation": "A race condition occurs when program correctness depends on non-deterministic interleaving of unsynchronized reads/writes."}, 84)
    add("ex_os_05", "operating_systems", "mod_csl301_3", "short", 2,
        "What four conditions must simultaneously hold for a system deadlock to occur according to Coffman?",
        {"correct": "Mutual exclusion, Hold and wait, No preemption, Circular wait",
         "rubric": "mutual exclusion hold wait no preemption circular wait coffman",
         "explanation": "The four Coffman conditions are Mutual Exclusion, Hold and Wait, No Preemption, and Circular Wait."}, 84)
    add("ex_os_06", "operating_systems", "mod_csl301_3", "mcq", 3,
        "What algorithm tests whether allocating resources to a requesting process preserves a safe state before granting the request?",
        {"options": ["Banker's algorithm", "Peterson's algorithm", "Dekker's algorithm", "Lamport's bakery algorithm"],
         "correct": "Banker's algorithm",
         "explanation": "Dijkstra's Banker's Algorithm evaluates resource allocation graphs/matrices to guarantee the system remains in a safe state."}, 84)
    add("ex_os_07", "operating_systems", "mod_csl301_3", "mcq", 3,
        "What is the phenomenon called when an OS spends more time paging data between RAM and swap space than executing user instructions?",
        {"options": ["Thrashing", "Pipelining", "Spooling", "Fragmentation"],
         "correct": "Thrashing",
         "explanation": "Thrashing occurs when working sets of active processes exceed physical RAM, causing constant page fault disk I/O."}, 84)
    add("ex_os_08", "operating_systems", "mod_csl301_2", "code", 3,
        "Implement a thread-safe counter increment function using Python threading.Lock.",
        {"correct": "Thread safe counter",
         "explanation": "Uses with lock: context manager to ensure atomic update of counter variable.",
         "solution": "import threading\nlock = threading.Lock()\ncounter = 0\ndef increment():\n    global counter\n    with lock:\n        counter += 1\n    return counter"}, 84,
        code="import threading\nlock = threading.Lock()\ncounter = 0\ndef increment():\n    # Increment counter safely using lock\n    pass")
    add("ex_os_09", "operating_systems", "mod_csl301_3", "mcq", 4,
        "What is Belady's Anomaly in operating systems page replacement?",
        {"options": ["Under FIFO page replacement, increasing allocated physical page frames can increase the number of page faults",
                     "Under LRU page replacement, page faults double on sorted access",
                     "Virtual addresses exceed physical memory capacity",
                     "Deadlocks occur between paging daemons and kernel threads"],
         "correct": "Under FIFO page replacement, increasing allocated physical page frames can increase the number of page faults",
         "explanation": "Belady's Anomaly is the counterintuitive property where FIFO replacement suffers more page faults with more memory frames."}, 84)
    add("ex_os_10", "operating_systems", "mod_csl301_2", "mcq", 4,
        "How does Peterson's algorithm guarantee mutual exclusion between two cooperating processes?",
        {"options": ["Combines process intent flags (flag[i] = true) with a shared 'turn' variable yielding to the other process",
                     "Uses atomic hardware Test-And-Set instructions exclusively",
                     "Disables interrupts across all CPU cores",
                     "Relies on OS kernel message queues"],
         "correct": "Combines process intent flags (flag[i] = true) with a shared 'turn' variable yielding to the other process",
         "explanation": "Peterson's algorithm achieves software mutual exclusion using two flags and a turn variable that breaks ties fairly."}, 84)

    # 9. compiler_design (CSL302, p. 84)
    add("ex_cd_01", "compiler_design", "mod_csl302_1", "mcq", 1,
        "Which compiler phase reads a stream of source characters and outputs a sequence of lexical tokens?",
        {"options": ["Lexical Analysis (Scanner)", "Syntax Analysis (Parser)", "Semantic Analysis", "Code Generator"],
         "correct": "Lexical Analysis (Scanner)",
         "explanation": "Lexical analysis converts raw characters into categorized tokens (e.g., IDENTIFIER, NUMBER, KEYWORD)."}, 84)
    add("ex_cd_02", "compiler_design", "mod_csl302_1", "mcq", 1,
        "What data structure is produced by the syntax analysis phase to capture hierarchical grammatical structure?",
        {"options": ["Abstract Syntax Tree (AST)", "Symbol Table only", "Control Flow Graph", "Three-Address Code"],
         "correct": "Abstract Syntax Tree (AST)",
         "explanation": "The parser constructs a parse tree or simplified Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) validating grammar conformance."}, 84)
    add("ex_cd_03", "compiler_design", "mod_csl302_2", "mcq", 2,
        "In the classification of LL(1) parsers, what do the two 'L's and the number '1' denote?",
        {"options": ["Left-to-right scan, Leftmost derivation, 1 lookahead token",
                     "Left-to-right scan, Linear time, 1 pass",
                     "Lexical lookahead, Left recursion, 1 symbol",
                     "Language level, Local optimization, 1 table"],
         "correct": "Left-to-right scan, Leftmost derivation, 1 lookahead token",
         "explanation": "LL(1) parses Left-to-right, constructs a Leftmost derivation, using 1 token of lookahead."}, 84)
    add("ex_cd_04", "compiler_design", "mod_csl302_2", "mcq", 2,
        "Why must immediate left recursion (A -> A alpha | beta) be eliminated before constructing a predictive top-down parser?",
        {"options": ["It causes recursive descent parser procedures to enter an infinite loop",
                     "It makes the grammar ambiguous",
                     "It prevents intermediate code generation",
                     "It prevents syntax directed translation"],
         "correct": "It causes recursive descent parser procedures to enter an infinite loop",
         "explanation": "A top-down parser calling parse_A() on A -> A alpha immediately calls parse_A() without consuming input tokens."}, 84)
    add("ex_cd_05", "compiler_design", "mod_csl302_2", "short", 2,
        "Given grammar production S -> 'a' B | epsilon, what is the FIRST set of non-terminal S?",
        {"correct": "{'a', epsilon}",
         "rubric": "a epsilon first set terminal set",
         "explanation": "FIRST(S) includes terminal 'a' from first alternative and epsilon from second alternative: {'a', epsilon}."}, 84)
    add("ex_cd_06", "compiler_design", "mod_csl302_3", "mcq", 3,
        "What is a shift-reduce conflict in bottom-up LR parser state tables?",
        {"options": ["The parser cannot decide whether to shift the next input token onto the stack or reduce by a production rule",
                     "The parser cannot decide which of two non-terminals to reduce",
                     "The grammar contains left recursion",
                     "The input string is empty"],
         "correct": "The parser cannot decide whether to shift the next input token onto the stack or reduce by a production rule",
         "explanation": "A shift-reduce conflict occurs when both a valid shift and a valid reduction are permissible in the current state."}, 84)
    add("ex_cd_07", "compiler_design", "mod_csl302_3", "mcq", 3,
        "What linearized intermediate representation format restricts every instruction to at most one operator and three operands?",
        {"options": ["Three-Address Code (TAC)", "PostScript", "Bytecode", "Static Single Assignment (SSA)"],
         "correct": "Three-Address Code (TAC)",
         "explanation": "Three-Address Code formats expressions as x = y op z, simplifying instruction selection and optimization."}, 84)
    add("ex_cd_08", "compiler_design", "mod_csl302_4", "mcq", 3,
        "In compiler optimization, what defines a 'Basic Block' in a Control Flow Graph (CFG)?",
        {"options": ["A maximal sequence of consecutive instructions with entry only at the first and exit only at the last",
                     "A loop body containing no function calls",
                     "A function definition with no local variables",
                     "A sequence of machine instructions executed in parallel"],
         "correct": "A maximal sequence of consecutive instructions with entry only at the first and exit only at the last",
         "explanation": "A basic block has a single entry point and single exit point; if the first instruction executes, all execute sequentially."}, 84)
    add("ex_cd_09", "compiler_design", "mod_csl302_3", "mcq", 4,
        "How does a Simple LR (SLR(1)) parser table construction resolve reductions in an LR(0) state?",
        {"options": ["Reduces by A -> alpha only if the lookahead symbol is in FOLLOW(A)",
                     "Reduces on all terminal symbols unconditionally",
                     "Reduces only on the end-of-input marker $",
                     "Uses full LR(1) item context propagation"],
         "correct": "Reduces by A -> alpha only if the lookahead symbol is in FOLLOW(A)",
         "explanation": "SLR(1) inspects FOLLOW(A) to avoid placing reduce actions into columns where A could never legally appear."}, 84)
    add("ex_cd_10", "compiler_design", "mod_csl302_4", "mcq", 4,
        "In Static Single Assignment (SSA) form, what special pseudo-operation merges values of a variable from converging control flow paths?",
        {"options": ["Phi (phi) function", "Mu (mu) function", "Delta function", "Branch join operator"],
         "correct": "Phi (phi) function",
         "explanation": "SSA uses phi-functions at basic block join points: x_3 = phi(x_1, x_2) selecting value based on preceding block."}, 84)

    # 10. database_systems (CSL303, p. 85)
    add("ex_db_01", "database_systems", "mod_csl303_1", "mcq", 1,
        "What does SQL stand for in database management systems?",
        {"options": ["Structured Query Language", "Standard Question Language", "Sequential Query Logic", "Systematic Quality Language"],
         "correct": "Structured Query Language",
         "explanation": "SQL stands for Structured Query Language, the ANSI/ISO standard declarative language for relational databases."}, 85)
    add("ex_db_02", "database_systems", "mod_csl303_1", "mcq", 1,
        "In relational database theory, what attribute or minimal set of attributes uniquely identifies each tuple in a relation?",
        {"options": ["Primary Key", "Foreign Key", "Index Key", "Composite View"],
         "correct": "Primary Key",
         "explanation": "A primary key enforces entity integrity by uniquely identifying every row in a table with non-null values."}, 85)
    add("ex_db_03", "database_systems", "mod_csl303_2", "mcq", 2,
        "Which relational normal form requires that every non-key attribute is fully functionally dependent on the primary key, eliminating partial dependencies?",
        {"options": ["Second Normal Form (2NF)", "First Normal Form (1NF)", "Third Normal Form (3NF)", "Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF)"],
         "correct": "Second Normal Form (2NF)",
         "explanation": "2NF requires 1NF plus the elimination of partial dependencies where non-prime attributes depend on a proper subset of candidate key."}, 85)
    add("ex_db_04", "database_systems", "mod_csl303_2", "mcq", 2,
        "What result does an SQL INNER JOIN between tables A and B produce?",
        {"options": ["Only rows where there is a match in both tables based on the join predicate",
                     "All rows from table A and only matching rows from table B",
                     "All rows from both tables including non-matching rows filled with NULLs",
                     "The Cartesian product of both tables unconditionally"],
         "correct": "Only rows where there is a match in both tables based on the join predicate",
         "explanation": "INNER JOIN discards rows from either table that have no corresponding matching key in the other table."}, 85)
    add("ex_db_05", "database_systems", "mod_csl303_3", "short", 2,
        "What four fundamental properties constitute the ACID transaction standard in database systems?",
        {"correct": "Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability",
         "rubric": "atomicity consistency isolation durability acid transaction",
         "explanation": "ACID stands for Atomicity (all or nothing), Consistency (preserves invariants), Isolation (serializable concurrent execution), and Durability (committed changes persist)."}, 85)
    add("ex_db_06", "database_systems", "mod_csl303_2", "mcq", 3,
        "In Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF), for every non-trivial functional dependency X -> Y, what must X be?",
        {"options": ["A superkey of the relation", "A foreign key", "A single atomic attribute", "A primary key column in another table"],
         "correct": "A superkey of the relation",
         "explanation": "BCNF strictly mandates that the determinant X in every non-trivial functional dependency must be a superkey."}, 85)
    add("ex_db_07", "database_systems", "mod_csl303_3", "mcq", 3,
        "What concurrency control protocol guarantees conflict serializability by dividing lock operations into an expanding phase and a shrinking phase?",
        {"options": ["Two-Phase Locking (2PL)", "Timestamp Ordering", "Validation-based Concurrency", "Multi-version Concurrency Control"],
         "correct": "Two-Phase Locking (2PL)",
         "explanation": "In 2PL, a transaction may acquire locks during the growing phase but cannot acquire any new lock once it releases its first lock."}, 85)
    add("ex_db_08", "database_systems", "mod_csl303_2", "code", 3,
        "Write an SQL query to retrieve department_id and average salary from employees table where average salary exceeds 50000.",
        {"correct": "GROUP BY and HAVING query",
         "explanation": "Aggregates with AVG(salary) grouped by department_id and filtered with HAVING clause.",
         "solution": "SELECT department_id, AVG(salary) FROM employees GROUP BY department_id HAVING AVG(salary) > 50000;"}, 85,
        code="-- Write SQL query using GROUP BY and HAVING\n")
    add("ex_db_09", "database_systems", "mod_csl303_4", "mcq", 4,
        "In database recovery management, what core rule does the Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) protocol mandate?",
        {"options": ["The log record describing an update must be flushed to stable storage before the corresponding dirty data page is written to disk",
                     "All transactions must commit in memory before logs are written",
                     "Data pages are written to disk before log records",
                     "Checkpoints occur only when database is offline"],
         "correct": "The log record describing an update must be flushed to stable storage before the corresponding dirty data page is written to disk",
         "explanation": "WAL guarantees that should a crash occur, uncommitted changes can be undone and committed changes redone from disk logs."}, 85)
    add("ex_db_10", "database_systems", "mod_csl303_3", "mcq", 4,
        "How is conflict serializability of a concurrent transactional schedule formally determined?",
        {"options": ["The precedence (serialization) graph constructed from conflicting operations contains no directed cycles",
                     "Every transaction completes before the next begins",
                     "No transaction requests exclusive locks",
                     "All write operations precede read operations"],
         "correct": "The precedence (serialization) graph constructed from conflicting operations contains no directed cycles",
         "explanation": "A schedule is conflict serializable iff its precedence graph (edges T_i -> T_j for conflicting operations) is acyclic."}, 85)

    # 11. artificial_intelligence (CSL304, p. 85)
    add("ex_ai_01", "artificial_intelligence", "mod_csl304_1", "mcq", 1,
        "What distinguishes an informed search algorithm from an uninformed (blind) search algorithm?",
        {"options": ["Informed search uses domain-specific heuristic functions estimating distance to the goal",
                     "Informed search does not maintain a frontier queue",
                     "Uninformed search is always faster than informed search",
                     "Informed search searches backwards from the goal only"],
         "correct": "Informed search uses domain-specific heuristic functions estimating distance to the goal",
         "explanation": "Heuristic functions h(n) estimate remaining cost, guiding informed search algorithms towards the goal more efficiently."}, 85)
    add("ex_ai_02", "artificial_intelligence", "mod_csl304_1", "mcq", 1,
        "Under what mathematical condition is the A* tree search algorithm guaranteed to return an optimal (least-cost) path?",
        {"options": ["The heuristic function h(n) is admissible (never overestimates the true remaining cost to goal)",
                     "The heuristic function h(n) is always greater than true cost",
                     "Step costs are all equal to zero",
                     "The search space contains no cycles"],
         "correct": "The heuristic function h(n) is admissible (never overestimates the true remaining cost to goal)",
         "explanation": "An admissible heuristic h(n) <= h*(n) guarantees that A* never prematurely expands suboptimal goal nodes."}, 85)
    add("ex_ai_03", "artificial_intelligence", "mod_csl304_2", "mcq", 2,
        "In adversarial game tree search, what is the primary benefit of Alpha-Beta pruning over standard Minimax?",
        {"options": ["Prunes subtrees that cannot influence the final root decision, reducing effective branching factor without sacrificing optimality",
                     "Changes the game outcome in favor of the maximizing player",
                     "Allows evaluation of non-deterministic dice rolls",
                     "Eliminates the need for a terminal evaluation function"],
         "correct": "Prunes subtrees that cannot influence the final root decision, reducing effective branching factor without sacrificing optimality",
         "explanation": "Alpha-beta pruning skips branches provably worse than previously discovered options, achieving up to 2x depth exploration."}, 85)
    add("ex_ai_04", "artificial_intelligence", "mod_csl304_2", "mcq", 2,
        "What property defines a consistent (or monotonic) heuristic in A* graph search?",
        {"options": ["For every node n and successor n' generated by action a, h(n) <= c(n, a, n') + h(n') and h(goal) = 0",
                     "h(n) >= c(n, a, n')",
                     "h(n) is constant across all nodes",
                     "h(n) equals the path cost g(n)"],
         "correct": "For every node n and successor n' generated by action a, h(n) <= c(n, a, n') + h(n') and h(goal) = 0",
         "explanation": "Consistency satisfies the triangle inequality, guaranteeing that f(n) non-decreases along any path and nodes are expanded optimally."}, 85)
    add("ex_ai_05", "artificial_intelligence", "mod_csl304_3", "short", 2,
        "What fundamental difference separates supervised machine learning from unsupervised machine learning?",
        {"correct": "labeled vs unlabeled data",
         "rubric": "supervised uses ground truth labels target outputs unsupervised finds patterns clusters unlabeled data",
         "explanation": "Supervised learning trains models on labeled input-output pairs; unsupervised learning discovers patterns and groupings in unlabeled data."}, 85)
    add("ex_ai_06", "artificial_intelligence", "mod_csl304_3", "mcq", 3,
        "In propositional resolution refutation, how is the validity of sentence KB |= alpha proved?",
        {"options": ["Convert KB and (not alpha) into Conjunctive Normal Form (CNF) and derive the empty clause (contradiction)",
                     "Show that KB and alpha are both true under truth tables",
                     "Prove that alpha contains no variables",
                     "Find a model where KB is false"],
         "correct": "Convert KB and (not alpha) into Conjunctive Normal Form (CNF) and derive the empty clause (contradiction)",
         "explanation": "Resolution refutation proves entailment by showing that asserting the negation of the query produces an unsatisfiable empty clause."}, 85)
    add("ex_ai_07", "artificial_intelligence", "mod_csl304_3", "mcq", 3,
        "What diagnostic signal indicates that a supervised machine learning model is overfitting the training dataset?",
        {"options": ["Very low training error accompanied by high test/validation generalization error",
                     "High training error and high test error simultaneously",
                     "Zero gradient during backpropagation",
                     "High learning rate instability"],
         "correct": "Very low training error accompanied by high test/validation generalization error",
         "explanation": "Overfitting occurs when a high-capacity model memorizes noise in the training set (high variance), failing to generalize to unseen test data."}, 85)
    add("ex_ai_08", "artificial_intelligence", "mod_csl304_4", "mcq", 3,
        "In Reinforcement Learning, what recursive equation expresses the value of a state as immediate reward plus discounted future state value?",
        {"options": ["Bellman Expectation Equation", "Bayes' Rule", "Navier-Stokes Equation", "Viterbi Equation"],
         "correct": "Bellman Expectation Equation",
         "explanation": "The Bellman equation decomposes the value function into immediate expected reward plus discounted continuation value gamma * V(s')."}, 85)
    add("ex_ai_09", "artificial_intelligence", "mod_csl304_2", "mcq", 4,
        "In Constraint Satisfaction Problems (CSPs), what constraint propagation algorithm maintains directional consistency across all variable arcs?",
        {"options": ["AC-3 (Arc Consistency Algorithm #3)", "Dijkstra's algorithm", "Minimax with alpha-beta", "K-means clustering"],
         "correct": "AC-3 (Arc Consistency Algorithm #3)",
         "explanation": "AC-3 iteratively prunes values from variable domains that have no valid supporting assignment in adjacent constrained variable domains."}, 85)
    add("ex_ai_10", "artificial_intelligence", "mod_csl304_4", "mcq", 4,
        "What does the Markov Property state regarding state transitions in a Markov Decision Process (MDP)?",
        {"options": ["The probability distribution over next states depends solely on the current state and action, independent of all past history",
                     "All states have equal probability of transition",
                     "The state transition matrix is symmetric",
                     "Rewards must be positive integers"],
         "correct": "The probability distribution over next states depends solely on the current state and action, independent of all past history",
         "explanation": "The Markov property states that conditional on the present, the future is independent of the past: P(S_{t+1}|S_t, A_t)."}, 85)

    # 12. computer_networks (CSL351, p. 85)
    add("ex_net_01", "computer_networks", "mod_csl351_1", "mcq", 1,
        "Which layer of the OSI architecture provides process-to-process communication and end-to-end reliability?",
        {"options": ["Transport Layer", "Network Layer", "Data Link Layer", "Physical Layer"],
         "correct": "Transport Layer",
         "explanation": "The transport layer (e.g. TCP, UDP) handles end-to-end process multiplexing via port numbers and flow control."}, 85)
    add("ex_net_02", "computer_networks", "mod_csl351_1", "mcq", 1,
        "What is the standard dotted-decimal subnet mask corresponding to a /24 IPv4 CIDR prefix?",
        {"options": ["255.255.255.0", "255.255.0.0", "255.255.255.128", "255.0.0.0"],
         "correct": "255.255.255.0",
         "explanation": "/24 indicates 24 leading ones in binary, which corresponds to 255.255.255.0."}, 85)
    add("ex_net_03", "computer_networks", "mod_csl351_2", "mcq", 2,
        "What sequence of packets establishes a reliable connection in the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP)?",
        {"options": ["SYN -> SYN-ACK -> ACK", "SYN -> ACK -> DATA", "HELLO -> ACK -> CONNECT", "FIN -> ACK -> FIN-ACK"],
         "correct": "SYN -> SYN-ACK -> ACK",
         "explanation": "TCP establishes state via the classic 3-way handshake: Client sends SYN, Server replies with SYN-ACK, Client confirms with ACK."}, 85)
    add("ex_net_04", "computer_networks", "mod_csl351_2", "mcq", 2,
        "What mathematical error-detecting polynomial division code is widely used in Ethernet frames at the Data Link layer?",
        {"options": ["Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC-32)", "Hamming (7, 4) Code", "Parity Bit", "MD5 Checksum"],
         "correct": "Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC-32)",
         "explanation": "CRC treats frame bits as polynomial coefficients and appends remainder bits from modulo-2 division by a generator polynomial."}, 85)
    add("ex_net_05", "computer_networks", "mod_csl351_3", "short", 2,
        "In an IPv4 subnetwork with CIDR block /28, how many usable host IP addresses are available?",
        {"correct": "14",
         "rubric": "14 usable host addresses 2^(32-28) - 2 = 16 - 2 = 14",
         "explanation": "A /28 subnet has 32 - 28 = 4 host bits: 2^4 = 16 total addresses minus network and broadcast addresses = 14 usable hosts."}, 85)
    add("ex_net_06", "computer_networks", "mod_csl351_3", "mcq", 3,
        "In TCP congestion control, how does the Slow Start phase adjust the congestion window (cwnd) upon receiving acknowledgments?",
        {"options": ["Doubles cwnd every Round-Trip Time (RTT) until reaching ssthresh",
                     "Increases cwnd by 1 MSS linearly per RTT",
                     "Decreases cwnd by half upon every ACK",
                     "Keeps cwnd constant until packet drop occurs"],
         "correct": "Doubles cwnd every Round-Trip Time (RTT) until reaching ssthresh",
         "explanation": "In slow start, cwnd increases by 1 MSS for each ACK received, which effectively doubles cwnd every RTT (exponential growth)."}, 85)
    add("ex_net_07", "computer_networks", "mod_csl351_3", "mcq", 3,
        "What problem in Distance Vector routing occurs when an unreachable destination creates routing loops that slowly increment metric values?",
        {"options": ["Count-to-Infinity problem", "Split Horizon problem", "Poison Reverse failure", "BGP flapping"],
         "correct": "Count-to-Infinity problem",
         "explanation": "The count-to-infinity problem occurs when routers exchange mutual advertisements for a failed link, incrementing distances step by step."}, 85)
    add("ex_net_08", "computer_networks", "mod_csl351_3", "mcq", 3,
        "In a Selective Repeat sliding window protocol with N-bit sequence numbers (total 2^N numbers), what is the maximum sender window size W?",
        {"options": ["2^(N - 1)", "2^N - 1", "2^N", "N^2"],
         "correct": "2^(N - 1)",
         "explanation": "To prevent overlap between the old and new sequence number spaces on ACK loss, window size must be <= half the sequence space: 2^(N-1)."}, 85)
    add("ex_net_09", "computer_networks", "mod_csl351_3", "mcq", 4,
        "How does the Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) guarantee loop-free inter-domain routing between Autonomous Systems?",
        {"options": ["Includes the full ordered sequence of AS numbers (AS-Path attribute) in route advertisements and discards routes containing own AS",
                     "Uses Dijkstra's algorithm across all global routers",
                     "Enforces a maximum hop count limit of 15",
                     "Broadcasts periodic distance vectors to all neighboring networks"],
         "correct": "Includes the full ordered sequence of AS numbers (AS-Path attribute) in route advertisements and discards routes containing own AS",
         "explanation": "As a path-vector protocol, BGP lists every AS traversed; an AS detecting its own ASN in the AS-Path immediately rejects the update."}, 85)
    add("ex_net_10", "computer_networks", "mod_csl351_3", "mcq", 4,
        "What security mechanism defends TCP servers against SYN Flood attacks by encoding connection state into the initial sequence number without allocating TCB memory?",
        {"options": ["SYN Cookies", "IPsec Tunneling", "TCP BBR", "Dynamic Port Randomization"],
         "correct": "SYN Cookies",
         "explanation": "SYN cookies cryptographically encode client IP, port, and timestamp into the server's SYN-ACK ISN, allocating memory only upon final ACK."}, 85)

    add("ex_se_04", "software_engineering", "mod_csl559_2", "mcq", 2,

    add("ex_se_05", "software_engineering", "mod_csl559_1", "short", 2,

    add("ex_se_06", "software_engineering", "mod_csl559_2", "mcq", 3,
        "In black-box software testing, what test generation technique focuses on values at the boundaries of equivalence partitions?",
        {"options": ["Boundary Value Analysis (BVA)", "Fuzz testing", "Mutation testing", "Static code analysis"],
         "correct": "Boundary Value Analysis (BVA)",
         "explanation": "BVA tests edge cases (e.g. min, min+1, max-1, max) where software defects statistically cluster most frequently."}, 90)
    add("ex_se_07", "software_engineering", "mod_csl559_2", "mcq", 3,
        "What architectural style structures an application as a collection of loosely coupled, independently deployable services organized around business capabilities?",
        {"options": ["Microservices architecture", "Monolithic architecture", "Client-Server architecture", "Peer-to-Peer architecture"],

    add("ex_se_08", "software_engineering", "mod_csl559_1", "mcq", 3,

    add("ex_se_09", "software_engineering", "mod_csl559_2", "mcq", 4,
        "What does Thomas McCabe's Cyclomatic Complexity metric measure in a program module?",
        {"options": ["The number of linearly independent paths through the control flow graph",
                     "The total number of physical lines of code (LOC)",
                     "The memory consumption of recursive call frames",
                     "The execution time in clock cycles"],
         "correct": "The number of linearly independent paths through the control flow graph",
         "explanation": "Cyclomatic complexity M = E - N + 2P calculates the number of decision points, guiding the minimum number of test cases required."}, 90)
    add("ex_se_10", "software_engineering", "mod_csl559_2", "mcq", 4,
        "What does the Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP) enforce regarding subclass behavioral subtyping?",
        {"options": ["Objects of a superclass should be replaceable with objects of a subclass without breaking program correctness or invariants",
                     "Subclasses must override every method of their parent class",
